 Judgment
Though the matter is listed for admission, with consent of learned Counsel on both side, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. "Whether the compensation awarded to the appellants by the Tribunal under the impugned award is just"? is the question involved in this case.
3. The appellants are the father and mother of the deceased Naveen.

On 20.03.2016 at 2.30 a.m.
when Naveen was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-EQ-6555 near Ganesh Temple,
Varthuru Main Road, car bearing No.KA-04-ME-3580 hit the motorcycle of Naveen.

In the accident,
Naveen suffered grievous injuries.
When he was being shifted to the hospital, he died on the way.
At the time of the accident, respondent No.1 was the Insurer and respondent No.2 was the owner of the car bearing No.KA-04-ME-3580.
4. The appellants filed MVC No.3494/2016 before MACT, Bengaluru (SCCH-14) against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.

The appellants alleged that they were dependents of the deceased Naveen, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver and due to the death of Naveen, they have lost their breadwinner.

5. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 contested the petition denying rashness and negligence on the part of the car driver, age, occupation, income of the deceased and their liability to pay the compensation.
6. The Tribunal on hearing the parties, by the impugned award held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the car.

The Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month, deducted  out of the same for his personal expenses, applied multiplier 18 and awarded total compensation of Rs.7,78,000/- under different heads as per the table below:

Sri K.V.Girish, learned Counsel for the appellants reiterating the grounds of the appeal submits that the income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side and the Tribunal committed error in not adding future prospects to the income of the deceased.

8. Sri H.S.Lingaraju, learned Counsel for the Insurer justifies the impugned award on the ground that there was no proof of income of the deceased, though the appellants contended that the deceased was working as Assistant Supervisor in Sri Vishnu Enterprises and earning Rs.22,400/-
per month, neither the said employer was examined nor Ex.P7 salary certificate was proved by examining the author of the same.
Therefore the Tribunal was justified in considering the income of the deceased notionally.
9. The accident took place in the year 2016.
Considering the age of the deceased, wage rate prevailing during the said period, income of Rs.6,000/- per month assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal should have considered the same at Rs.9,500/- per month.
10. Having regard to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi1, 40% has to be super added to the said income as future prospects.

11. Since the deceased was Bachelor, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation2,  of the income has to be deducted for his personal expenses.

sentences.text: Therefore his net monthly income comes to Rs.6,650/-.
The applicable multiplier is 18.
Therefore the just compensation payable under the head of loss of dependency is (Rs.6,650 x 12 x 18) = Rs.14,36,400/-.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case referred to supra, the appellants being parents of the deceased are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each on the head of consortium with escalation at 10% which comes to (Rs.44,000/- x 2)= 88,000/-.

Similarly in the light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case referred to supra, the appellants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on the head of funeral expenses and loss of estate with Vijaya Kumar M Julajuli vs M/S Bajaj Allianz General Insurnace Co ... on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115171430/

Therefore just compensation payable is as follows:

 2. Loss of consortium 88,000/-

3 . Loss of estate and funeral 33,000/-
 expenses
The Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 9% per annum on the compensation awarded.
Though Insurer has not preferred any appeal, in view of Section 34 of CPC, it is just and appropriate to award interest at 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation.
The award of the Tribunal is modified accordingly.
Therefore the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced by Rs.7,79,400/- with interest thereon at 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the said amount before the Tribunal within four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
The order of the Tribunal with regard to apportionment and investment is maintained.
